trust_decision.summary: The cluster engine decides whether a session id taken from an inter-node bus message (or a WebSocket query) names a locally owned client. It looks the id up on the plain object this.clients with bracket access, so inherited prototype keys count as clients.

landing_point.why: 'client session lookup' points straight to ClusterEngine.onMessage. Every lookup but one is in that switch, and the remaining one is 377 lines lower in the same file.

fix_sites.entry_point: bus message ACQUIRE_LOCK via NodeClusterEngine process 'message' (packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/lib/cluster.ts:48) or RedisEngine subscribe (packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/lib/redis.ts:147)
bus message PACKET via the same transports
bus message UPGRADE via the same transports
bus message CLOSE via the same transports
HTTP upgrade (handleUpgrade -> onWebSocket override), query param sid

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue the onWebSocket site (engine.ts:556) is already covered, because the base verify() rejects non-own sids with hasOwn (packages/engine.io/lib/server.ts:310) and the cluster verify only accepts 20-character sids (packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/lib/engine.ts:409). That argument is weak, since the published fix changes this site anyway.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A legitimate remote session id must still resolve. Cross-node lock acquisition, packet forwarding, upgrade takeover and close have to keep working for real own-keyed clients, and onWebSocket must still hand known sids to super.onWebSocket. An over-broad fix (for example rejecting every id in the bus handler, or switching to a Map without updating the base class) breaks clustering.

O6_input_shapes: sid naming an Object.prototype property (e.g. 'constructor', 'toString', '__proto__') in a bus message data.sid
same, in the WebSocket upgrade query sid

O8b_injection_room.sibling: _remoteTransports kept as a plain Record instead of a Map, so the DRAIN lookup at engine.ts:247 by message.data.sid becomes an unguarded prototype lookup
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: clients in the base class is already a Record with a TODO to move to Map (packages/engine.io/lib/server.ts:182-183), so a maintainer could easily have used the same shape for a sibling table. It is a WHERE-type sibling only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a uWS upgrade path that resolves req._query.sid before or without verify()'s hasOwn check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: userver.ts is a second server implementation (uWebSockets) of the same lookup, in another file from the cluster-engine landing point. Today it depends on the shared verify() at packages/engine.io/lib/server.ts:310.

O9_family: prototype pollution / unsafe own-property lookup on a plain-object map (CWE-20 / CWE-1321)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm workspaces, tsc, mocha with tsx (packages/socket.io-cluster-engine/package.json:26-32)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the case the report reproduces (e.g. ACQUIRE_LOCK at engine.ts:188) or add an isValidSessionId length check in onMessage. Either one leaves the PACKET/UPGRADE/CLOSE/onWebSocket lookups unguarded.

out_of_scope_notes: packages/engine.io/lib/server.ts:910-911 indexes the transports table with req._query.transport, but verify() already restricts transport to opts.transports (packages/engine.io/lib/server.ts:288). Not pursued.
packages/socket.io-client/lib/socket.ts:809 looks up acks[packet.id] on the client side. Different package and different trust direction. Not pursued.
